lessons.title: The four questions
lessons.body:
Threat modeling is just a disciplined way to ask, of anything you build:
  1. What are we building?        (model the system)
  2. What can go wrong?           (find the threats)
  3. What are we going to do?     (mitigate them)
  4. Did we do a good job?        (check your work)
That's the whole method. For Vantaris AI it's how you derive the hit points BEFORE you start breaking things - instead of poking randomly, you model the system, enumerate what can go wrong at each part, and turn each threat into a mission. Threat modeling is the map; the missions are you walking it.

lessons.title: STRIDE - what can go wrong
lessons.body:
STRIDE is a checklist of the six things that go wrong, each the violation of one security property:
  Spoofing                -> breaks Authentication   (pretending to be someone)
  Tampering               -> breaks Integrity        (changing data/code)
  Repudiation             -> breaks Non-repudiation   (denying you did it)
  Information disclosure   -> breaks Confidentiality   (leaking data)
  Denial of service       -> breaks Availability      (knocking it offline)
  Elevation of privilege   -> breaks Authorization      (gaining rights)
Walk each component and ask 'which of these apply?'. Our missions ARE STRIDE: crack-01 is Spoofing (stolen creds), app-01 SQLi is Tampering + Information disclosure + Elevation of privilege, bin-01 defeats a check (Tampering/EoP), wire-01 is about catching it so the attacker can't repudiate.

lessons.title: Data flow diagrams and trust boundaries
lessons.body:
To find threats you first draw the system as a data flow diagram with four shapes:
  - external entities (users, other systems)   - squares
  - processes (your code, the app, the agent)   - circles
  - data stores (SQL Server, files, the index)  - parallel lines
  - data flows (requests, queries, documents)   - arrows
Then draw TRUST BOUNDARIES: lines where data crosses from less-trusted to more-trusted (browser -> app, app -> SQL Server, a customer's uploaded doc -> the RAG index). Threats cluster on those boundaries. Vantaris's boundaries: the internet edge, the app-to-database link, the AD domain edge, and - the new one - untrusted content flowing into the AI agent.

lessons.title: What to do about a threat
lessons.body:
For every threat you have four responses:
  Mitigate  - add a control that makes it hard (parameterize the query, add MFA)
  Eliminate - remove the feature/asset entirely (don't store what you don't need)
  Transfer  - make it someone else's job (managed service, insurance, a contract)
  Accept    - decide the risk is tolerable and document that decision
The blue-team twin of each mission is you MITIGATING: break it, then add the control and prove it holds. 'Did we do a good job?' means every element of the diagram and every STRIDE category has an answer - that completeness is what a real assessment delivers.

lessons.title: Threat modeling the AI product
lessons.body:
The RAG agent is Vantaris's crown jewel and its newest attack surface, so run STRIDE on it directly:
  Tampering             -> prompt injection: untrusted text in a document becomes instructions the agent follows
  Information disclosure -> the agent retrieves and reveals data the user wasn't allowed to see (oversharing / weak row-level security)
  Elevation of privilege -> an over-permissioned agent identity does more than the user could (the text-to-SQL agent running as db_owner)
  Spoofing / Repudiation -> who did the agent act as, and is it logged?
The trust boundary that matters most: the one between RETRIEVED CONTENT and the agent's INSTRUCTIONS. Treat retrieved text as data, never as commands - that single boundary is the heart of the capstone.

quiz.q: Which STRIDE category does SQL injection that dumps a secret table MOST represent?
quiz.why: Reading data you shouldn't is Information disclosure (it's also Tampering/EoP).

quiz.q: Stolen or cracked credentials are which STRIDE threat?
quiz.why: Using someone's creds is impersonation = Spoofing (breaks authentication).
Trust boundaries - where data moves from less- to more-trusted - are where to look.

quiz.q: Prompt injection against the RAG agent is best described as...
quiz.why: Retrieved/untrusted text crosses into the instruction flow and is obeyed - Tampering.
